title: AI Debaters are More Persuasive when Arguing in Alignment with Their Own Beliefs

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting debater models to select a stance when facing a judge persona explicitly designed to conflict with the models' established prior beliefs, and measuring the rate of stance changes to align with the judge to maximize persuasiveness.
Evaluating the empirical win counts of the second debater in a sequential debate setup against a binomial null distribution to detect if argument order systematically advantages one debater.

Analyzing the consistency of judge models in selecting the same stance across repeated trials of a subjective scenario to evaluate how strongly the judge's pre-existing beliefs influence their verdict compared to the provided arguments.
